title: Rust slot.rs from_cose accepts non-ascending payload keys and trailing payload bytes (violates adjudicated deterministic-CBOR contract)
description: Codereview finding on 5rfl (reviewer kimi-k3, 3 passes, empirically PoC-confirmed). Rust RawSlotClaim::from_cose (rust/lichen-gateway/src/slot.rs:559-594) iterates payload map keys in arrival order — the seen bitmask rejects duplicates/unknown/missing but nothing enforces ascending key order — and never calls p.finished() on the payload reader (the finished() check at slot.rs:543 covers only the outer envelope), so it accepts <canonical map><garbage>. spec/decisions.jsonl id slot-claim-cose-sign1 (Mark, 2026-09-03) adjudicated the payload as deterministic-CBOR, so this leniency is the spec violation. Divergence today: a signature-valid claim with permuted keys or trailing payload bytes is ACCEPTED by Rust (its verifier digests the canonical re-encode, slot.rs:621-626, so the sig still verifies) while Python (5rfl byte-equality gate, decode_cose) and C (digests the RECEIVED payload bytes, coap_slot_coord.c:394) reject both forms — a relay can flip Python/C vs Rust verdicts with zero key material. Fix: in from_cose, require strictly ascending payload keys (monotonic last-key check) and p.finished() after the 7-pair map, matching Reader::head minimality already enforced in tunnel_auth.rs:745-775. Add Rust-side wire tests for reordered keys + trailing bytes; both must become MalformedClaim. Adjacent but NOT duplicate: l1qw.16.2 (resources.rs wiring leg), ga0p/w1j4 (SCHC/C trailing bytes, other subsystems).
